A 20-year-old male patient is seen for a follow-up evaluation six weeks after being hospitalized for
alcohol-induced acute pancreatitis. His hospital course was complicated by respiratory distress
requiring ICU admission and poor nutritional status necessitating nasojejunal feeding. Currently, the
patient reports feeling well with only mild abdominal fullness and is successfully maintaining a low-fat
diet with positive weight gain. His physical examination reveals normal temperature and blood
pressure. A CT scan of the abdomen demonstrates inflammatory changes in the peripancreatic region
and reveals a newly developed 5-cm fluid-filled mass with thick walls adjacent to the pancreatic body.
What is the most appropriate management approach for this patient's condition? Answer Choices: (A)
Surgical cyst removal (B) Aspiration and culture of the cyst fluid (C) Antibiotic therapy (D) Total
parenteral nutrition (E) Percutaneous catheter drainage (F) Endoscopic drainage (G) Intravenous
corticosteroids (H) Endoscopic cystogastrostomy (I) Watchful waiting (J) Immediate surgical
debridement
 A. Intravenous corticosteroids
B. Endoscopic cystogastrostomy
C. Total parenteral nutrition
D. Percutaneous catheter drainage
E. Antibiotic therapy
F. Surgical cyst removal
G. Watchful waiting
H. Endoscopic drainage
I. Aspiration and culture of the cyst fluid
J. Immediate surgical debridement
